title: A wine merchant
text: Wine from Gascony, a tun at a time. The king takes his prise from every cargo, and the town takes its toll. But a man who knows the tides, and Bordeaux, does well enough.
speaker: p254

title: Burgesses of the town
text: Bristol has its charters, and a mayor of its own since 1216. We make our own rules here, and we pay the king well for the right to.
speaker: p256

title: A family come to market
text: We walked in at dawn with eggs and a cheese. Then there's the toll at the gate, and the fee for a place at the market. What's left buys salt, and maybe a little cloth.
speaker: p257

title: The bridge-ward
text: Every cart that crosses pays toward the bridge. Without the tolls it would fall, and the town would be cut in two.
speaker: p259

title: A guard at the castle
text: This is the king's castle, not the town's. Go in if you have business here, friend, but keep a civil tongue, and your hands to yourself.
speaker: p278

title: A guard inside the castle gate
text: You're in the king's castle now. Bow to the constable if you meet him, keep out of the soldiers' way, and mind your step.
speaker: p273

title: A watchman
text: When the curfew bell rings, the gates are shut and the watch keeps the streets. A stranger abroad at night had better have a good reason.
speaker: p245

title: The town crier
text: The mayor's orders, the king's news, and every lost purse and strayed pig. If it's cried in the market, nobody can say they weren't told.
speaker: p232

title: The ostler
text: Horses for hire, by the day, fed and shod. A merchant who must be in Bath by noon pays what I ask, and is glad to.
speaker: p286
